# #1903: Patch: the networked e2e specs take their api, bearer and session helpers from support
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Fifteen Cypress specs that talk to the server each carry a private copy of the same two tiny helpers — one that builds an API URL, one that builds an auth header — several re-declare the session-storage key that support already exports, and a few hand-roll a visit-with-session helper that the shared `cy.visitAs` already provides. After this they all import the one shared implementation: no behaviour change, roughly 115 fewer lines, and one place to fix if the session shape ever moves.

## Why

Identical `function api(path: string)` + `function bearer(account)` pair in 15 spec files (`05-reconnect` through `45-economy-loop`); `SESSION_STORAGE_KEY` re-declared in 4-6 specs though `e2e/support/config.ts:56` exports it; a hand-rolled `visitAs` in 4 specs duplicates `commands.ts:842-885` (`cy.visitAs`/`cy.signIn`/`carrySession`, which already preserves session-write ordering before a caller's `onBeforeLoad`). Mirrors the accepted web-test dedup (#1814).

## Proposal

Export `apiUrl`/`bearerHeaders` from `e2e/support/config.ts`, use `cy.visitAs` (with an `onBeforeLoad` passthrough for `39-replays`' download spy) everywhere, and import `SESSION_STORAGE_KEY`.

## Where it lands

`e2e/cypress/e2e/*.cy.ts` (~19 files), `e2e/support/config.ts:46-56`, `e2e/support/commands.ts:815-885`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No spec declares its own `api`, `bearer`, `visitAs` or `SESSION_STORAGE_KEY`.
- [ ] Touched specs behave identically — the same URL string, header record and session JSON shape.
- [ ] `pnpm exec cypress run` on the touched specs against the `E2E=1` server (daily suite covers all).

## Size and risks

Medium, difficulty medium: ~19 files, ~115 net lines deleted; e2e-only, no production code. Risk: keeping each spec's exact mount/write ordering — mechanical, caught by running the specs.

- [ ] `config.ts` exports `apiUrl` and `bearerHeaders`; `commands.ts` and all 15 specs import them, and none defines its own.
- [ ] 05, 06, 10 and 39 have no `SESSION_STORAGE_KEY` and no `visitAs` of their own, and call `cy.visitAs`.

- [ ] Step 7's grep prints nothing.
- [ ] Both typechecks and `pnpm exec eslint e2e` pass.
- [ ] Every touched spec passes `cypress run`, or each failure is reported with its output next to the same spec's run at the base.
- [ ] The README paragraph is added.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass.

- **A visit that now carries a session.** `cy.visitAs` remembers its account for the rest of the spec file (`signedIn` in `commands.ts`), and every later `cy.visit` installs that session. Keep it that way: add no other plain visit.
- **Write order.** `carrySession` writes the session and then runs the caller's `onBeforeLoad`, which is the order 39's hand-rolled helper used. Pass `spyOnDownloads` itself, not a wrapper that writes the session again.
- **Unused imports.** Removing `api` leaves the `server` import unused in 09, 10, 18, 26, 40 and 44. The word "server" still appears in those files' comments, but no code there calls `server.`. CI's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule fails on an unused import, which is why Steps 3 and 4 remove it.
- **A rename that hits something else.** None of the 16 files has any other `api(`, `.api(` or `bearer(`. Run each `sed` only on the files its step names.
- **Chrome 155's network-service crash** can fail a spec at random with "Couldn't reach JackiOh". `E2E_CHROME_PIN=1` avoids it if Chrome for Testing downloads. If it doesn't, re-run that one spec once before treating the failure as real, and report it.
- Nothing here touches hidden information, rules, replays or determinism: it is test code only.

## Open questions

- **Left out on purpose.** Specs 27 and 35 keep their own `headers()` helper and their inline `${server.http()}/api/…` URLs. The issue's acceptance names only `api`, `bearer`, `visitAs` and `SESSION_STORAGE_KEY`, so they are out of scope. Spec 99 (the online smoke, which hits real servers with an `Authorization` header) and `support/tasks/stayQueued.ts` (which runs in Node) also stay as they are. A person may want 27 and 35 moved onto `apiUrl`/`bearerHeaders` in a follow-up.
- **Decision: `bearerHeaders` takes a token string.** That matches the copy already in `commands.ts`; the cost is that the specs that passed an account add `.token` at each call. Two alternatives were rejected:
  - Taking an `E2EAccount`: that would mean restructuring 06's `{ token }` seat loop, and 10's `pendingToken()` and `me(token)`.
  - Taking `E2EAccount | string`: that gives one helper two shapes.
